subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Facial Recognition in Public
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Facial Recognition in Public.

hook.text: Walk down a city street. A camera scans your face, matches it to a database, and identifies you in seconds.

buildup.text: Facial recognition compares your features against millions of photos using AI-powered pattern matching.

discovery.text: Clearview AI scraped over 30 billion photos from social media to build a facial recognition tool for police.

twist.text: Studies show the technology misidentifies Black and Asian faces at rates 10 to 100 times higher than white faces.

climax.text: A technology that's biased, unregulated, and used by police to identify people in public spaces without consent.

punchline.text: Scanned without consent. Biased by design.

quiz.question: What racial bias has been documented in facial recognition technology?
options: It misidentifies Black and Asian faces at much higher rates
It only works accurately on faces under age 30
No bias has been found in modern systems
